questions.question: What is a pidgin?
options: A simplified contact language that emerges when speakers of different languages need to communicate
A language with native speakers and full grammar
An extinct ancient language
A secret code used by sailors only
questions.explanation: A pidgin is a simplified contact language developed for practical communication - typically trade - between groups with no common language.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a pidgin and a creole?
options: A creole has native speakers and a full grammar, while a pidgin is nobody's mother tongue
A pidgin is older than all creoles
A creole is always written, a pidgin always spoken
There is no difference
questions.explanation: When children grow up speaking a pidgin as their first language, it expands into a creole - a complete natural language with native speakers.

questions.question: Are creoles considered "real" languages by linguists?
options: Yes - they are natural human languages with complete grammars
No - they are just broken English
Only if they are written down
Only in Europe
questions.explanation: Linguistically, creoles are unequivocally full languages capable of expressing any thought, although they often suffer from low social prestige.

questions.question: In what historical context did many English-based creoles develop?
options: Colonial trade and plantation slavery, where speakers of many languages were brought together
Medieval monasteries
The space race
The invention of printing
questions.explanation: Many creoles, such as Jamaican Creole, arose on plantations where enslaved people speaking different languages developed common contact languages.

questions.question: Why do creoles often have low social status despite being full languages?
options: They are socially stigmatized and often viewed as "broken" versions of the standard language
They lack grammar entirely
Their speakers refuse to use them
They cannot express abstract ideas
questions.explanation: Social prejudice, not linguistic deficiency, gives creoles low prestige: they are often wrongly dismissed as incorrect versions of English.
